entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:1
segments: The higher a man's standing and reputation, the more injurious to himself and others is the exhibition of folly.  A little foolishness may overshadow great wisdom.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:2
segments: At his right hand; he uses it skilfully.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:3
segments:
Walketh by the way; appears in public. 
 
  Saith to every one; by his actions. 
 
When folly appears in public it always betrays itself.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:5
segments: As an error which proceedeth; that is, an error such as proceedeth. The error consists in exalting the mean and unworthy to office, a common evil in the despotic governments of the East.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:6
segments:
The rich; the same as "princes" in the following verse, who unite wealth with nobleness and intelligence. 
 
The elevation of unworthy men to offices of power and trust is a heavy calamity to the people.  Whether it proceed from their rulers, or, as in the case of free governments, from themselves, the result will be corruption, misrule, and misery.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:8
segments:
vv 8-10. 
 
  He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it--wisdom is profitable to direct; general meaning: the dangers and difficulties of life are many; but wisdom is profitable to direct in them all.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:14
segments: It is often the case, that the less men have to say that will benefit themselves or others, the more they abound in words.  "A wise head makes a short tongue," is the true Arabic proverb.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:15
segments: How to go to the city; a particular instance of his ignorance, which stands to represent all other cases.  As much as to say, when he undertakes the simplest enterprise, he knows not how and where to find the means of success.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:16
segments: The primary qualification for ruling others is ability to rule ourselves.  They who destroy themselves by self-indulgence, will destroy also the people committed to their care.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:18
segments: The house droppeth through; lets water drop through the roof. Here, again, we have a particular case to illustrate a general principle.

entries.title: Ecclesiastes 10:20
segments: Vain is the hope of escaping punishment by the secrecy of our evil deeds.  God is able, in numberless unforeseen ways to bring them to light here, and he will expose them all hereafter in the presence of men and angels.
